## How it will work

- 1 Install on your GitHub org Pick all repositories or a few. The App asks for read-only access to contents and cannot change code.

### Install on your GitHub org

- 2 Scan against verified rules Each rule is an identifier pattern with the provider's shutdown date, the replacement and a link to the notice. A person checks each rule before it ships.

### Scan against verified rules

- 3 One issue per repository A rolling issue lists file:line, identifier, shutdown date, replacement and source. It updates as you fix things.

### One issue per repository

- 4 Checks on pull requests (Pro) A Check Run annotates pull requests that add a new reference to a retiring identifier, so old IDs don't creep back in.

### Checks on pull requests (Pro)

## What it doesn't do

- It doesn't open pull requests or edit code. It has no write access to contents.

- It doesn't guarantee complete coverage. It checks your code against the rules we have verified, and each rule links to its source.

- It doesn't support GitLab or Bitbucket.
